newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai hotel to end contract with Sheraton.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai hotel to end contract with Sheraton.

text.p: Shanghai's first and largest five-star hotel will not renew a 10-year management contract with the Sheraton group when it expires at the end of October 1997, an official of the hotel said on Thursday.
Asked if the hotel would employ foreigners after October 1997, the hotel official said that it might use some as chefs but declined further comment.

While the Sheraton Huating Hotel, which opened in November 1986, was satisfied with the current management, some of the methods seen as advanced in other countries were not entirely effective in China, the Liberation Daily newspaper reported on Thursday.
The Sheraton Huating Hotel opened in November 1986 with 1,000 rooms, of which 770 have been used for guests and the rest for hotel facilities and offices, the official told Reuters.
The Sheraton Huating belongs to the state-owned Huating Group.

An official of the Shanghai Tourism Administration said saving money on the management fee was a factor in the decision. But he said the city still welcomed foreign management of its hotels, adding the decision should not be seen as a trend.
